from.title: The Cambridge History of Western Music Theory

topics.title: Thoroughbass and partimento in the history of theory

attachTo.note: Context for the schemata and the rule of the octave.

points: Thoroughbass appears in print with Viadana (1602). Agazzari (1607) divides continuo instruments into those of foundation and those of ornament.
Partimento and "preluding" join bass-based improvisation to composition, above all in Naples.
Heinichen (1728) turns thoroughbass into a complete composition course, teaching styles through the figured bass.
Before Rameau, harmony was taught as patterns over the bass: Campion's rule (1618) and the rule of the octave.
Around 1800 three national traditions blend: French fundamental bass, Italian species counterpoint and partimento, and German thoroughbass.

terms.def: Accompaniment improvised over a figured bass.
Ornamental elaboration of a simple line into faster notes.
A bass (often unfigured) used to teach improvisation and composition, especially in Naples.
Improvised accompaniment from a bass line with figures; in Germany the core of composition teaching.
Rameau's bass of chord roots, the French analytical tradition.
A comprehensive "doctrine of composition" (Marx), including forms.
